# casting

### context: full
CASTING COST INPUT RULES:
  Lines marked deterministic are computed from the measured geometry and will REPLACE whatever you return for them — restate them, do not re-derive them.
  Lines marked UNDECIDED are yours to answer: nothing in the geometry settles them. Answer from the drawing, the photo or the part name, and say which you used.
  leak-tight question=no  [answered — deterministic, use verbatim]
  tolerance-class question=standard  [answered — deterministic, use verbatim]
  safety-critical question=no  [answered — deterministic, use verbatim]
  materialId=mat-lm25  [aluminium gravity casting → LM25 / A356 (A356 / LM25, the heat-treatable gravity / sand alloy — not a drawing callout) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  grade: UNDECIDED — needs "Which aluminium grade?" (EN AC-46200 (AlSi8Cu3, gravity / low-pressure — cylinder heads, housings) | LM4 / AlSi5Cu3 (secondary, sand / gravity) | LM6 / EN AC-44100 (AlSi12, gravity / sand) | LM25 / A356 | EN AC-51300 (AlMg5, marine sand / gravity) | LM13 / EN AC-48000 (AlSi12CuNiMg — pistons) | EN AC-45300 (AlSi5Cu1Mg / C355 — cylinder heads, T6) | A357 / AlSi7Mg0.6 (Premium T6) | A206 / AlCu4.5MgTi (high-strength premium casting))
  subtype=gravity  [gravity: medium-volume aluminium — gravity die casting gives denser, heat-treatable (T6) structure than HPDC for wheels/knuckles/pistons, with cheaper tooling than a pressure die — deterministic, use verbatim]
  yieldFraction=0.6  [gravity aluminium yield band 0.5–0.7, midpoint (feeding scales with the alloy's shrinkage; engineering-typical band, not sourced — the foundry's method yield replaces it) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  netWeightKg=2.8  [1037 cm³ × 0.0027 kg/cm³ (aluminium, confirmed by engineer) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldCostGBP=18144  [gravity die, toolmaker shop model: 223 toolroom hours + 124 kg of H13 (the die material is chosen with its life — H13 die, 100,000 die cycles a cavity — the upper half of D3 — Degarmo et al. (2003) via Wikipedia: permanent-mould life "10,000 to 120,000 cycles"; H13 "several times greater" than grey iron (B); D5 — US DOE / CWRU–AFS fact sheet (1999): wrought H13 is the best mould material in thermal fatigue; "selection … depends on the number of castings" (B); the choice of 100,000 is our inference (grade D)) + bought-outs from a 288 cm² parting footprint; 2 undercut face(s) ≈ 1 slide(s) a cavity priced as the moulding build-up prices a side action (a catalogue core-pull cylinder + bench hours a mechanism — no gravity-die slide price was read). Cross-check: D1 — Made-in-China (WuXi JingJie): H13 / P20 gravity mould for a motorcycle caliper US$3,800 a set (C; cavities and slides not stated). H13 hardening / nitriding is not itemised; mid-life maintenance (re-nitriding, coating touch-up, cavity inserts) is assumed done and NOT priced — no source gives its cost (research gap 3) — a quotation overrides this — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dieMouldLife=100000  [H13 die, 100,000 die cycles a cavity — the upper half of D3 — Degarmo et al. (2003) via Wikipedia: permanent-mould life "10,000 to 120,000 cycles"; H13 "several times greater" than grey iron (B); D5 — US DOE / CWRU–AFS fact sheet (1999): wrought H13 is the best mould material in thermal fatigue; "selection … depends on the number of castings" (B); the choice of 100,000 is our inference (grade D) × 1 impression = 100,000 castings a die (the die priced is H13); mid-life maintenance (re-nitriding, coating touch-up, cavity inserts) is assumed done and NOT priced — no source gives its cost (research gap 3). It was 50,000 castings (engineering-typical) on a die priced in cast iron — deterministic, use verbatim]
  cycleTimeSandGravHr=0.1445  [1 impression × 2.851 kg as cast ÷ 0.6 yield = 4.752 kg poured a die opening; die cycle = min(9, max(t_mass, t_section)): t_mass 3 + (4.8 − 3) × (4.752 − 3) ÷ (7.5 − 3) = 3.701 min (anchors: 3 min a small casting — G4 — MIRAE 2(2) 2025: small motorcycle accessory castings, 3.0 min a part on a manual station → 1.24 min mechanised (B); G2 — FMT (Hall, 2009): a single tilt-pour machine "12-30 cycles per hour" (2–5 min a die cycle); an indexing rotary table with tending robots run by one operator (C) — and 4.8 min, the former 0.08 h book figure, which matches G5 — Bonollo et al., La Metallurgia Italiana 6/2005: gravity die 0.15 h a casting for 6 kg and 13 kg castings, yield 0.80 / 0.73 (B) and G3 — Foundry-Planet (Gauss cell, Wuling, 2011): 11 cylinder heads an hour a machine, one operator "operates on four machines" (C)); t_section 3 × (17.00 ÷ 10)² = 8.670 min (Chvorinov — freezing ∝ section², the casting modulus 2·V/S); the 9 min ceiling is G5's 0.15 h. Linear between the mass anchors, 3 min at a 10 mm section and the max of the two: engineering-typical, not sourced → 8.670 min (the section term governs) = 0.1445 h a die opening. Replace with the foundry's cycle sheet — deterministic, use verbatim]
  labourId=lab-uk-foundry  [foundry operative on the moulding / die-casting line and at the fettling bench — deterministic, use verbatim]
  fettlingMinutes=2  [light fettling — gravity aluminium, 2.8 kg: gate / riser removal and grind at the foundry rate, 2 min (engineering-typical, not sourced — published manual times run from 45 s a small high-volume ductile casting (Malleable Castings time study) to 15–20 min a cylinder block (Mahindra, 2011)) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatTreatCostPerKg=0  [gravity aluminium T6: costed as a station (furnace kWh, operator and capital — see the heat treatment line), no £/kg here; a heat treater's £/kg typed here replaces the station — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heatTreatment=T6  [gravity aluminium is solution treated and aged — T6 costed until the heat-treat question is answered. ESTIMATE (grade D — a build-up, no toll price was found in any country): T6 (solution + quench + age) on a batch furnace set — H1 — Nanjing Boqiao "aluminum quenching furnace T6 heat treatment" set, Made-in-China product page: solution / quench furnace 150 + 7.5 + 5.5 kW, 1.5 t, empty heat-up 2.5 h; ageing furnace 30 kW, 1.5 t, empty heat-up 1.5 h; US$40,000–60,000 a set (C). Energy: solution 163.0 kW × (2.5 h heat-up + 6 h soak) × 0.6 = 831.3 kWh + age 30 kW × (1.5 h + 5 h) × 0.6 = 117.0 kWh = 948.3 kWh a load ÷ 1,000 kg net = 0.9483 kWh/kg of electricity, priced at the costed country's tariff. Furnace operator: 1 for the 8.5 h solution load cycle ÷ 1,000 kg = 0.0085 h/kg at the costed country's furnace-operator rate. Capital: US$40,000–60,000 midpoint ÷ 1.3344 $/£ = £37,470 (the set) = £37,470; £37,470 ÷ 10 yr + 3.5 % of it for maintenance a year (the library's line build-up rule) = £5058.45 a year ÷ (650 loads × 1,000 kg) = £0.007782/kg — a traded machine, at par in every country. Judgements (grade D): 6 h solution soak and 5 h age (ASM-typical A356 cycle, not read this round), 1,000 kg net of the 1.5 t gross load, 60 % average draw (55–65 %), 650 loads a year. Baskets, quench water and its treatment are NOT costed (no figure). A heat treater's £/kg typed as the heat-treat cost replaces the station. In this book: 0.9483 kWh/kg × £0.182/kWh + 0.0085 h/kg × £24.6/h + £0.007782/kg = £0.3895/kg before labour efficiency, × the as-cast kg — deterministic, use verbatim]
  heat-treat question: UNDECIDED — needs "Which heat treatment does the drawing call for on this aluminium casting?" (T6 — solution + quench + age | T5 — artificial age only | F — as cast, no heat treatment)
  gravityImpressions=1  [one impression (not answered — one costed; two would fit: 2 impressions of 320 × 240 mm (+50 mm a side, engineering-typical) fit the 800 × 600 mm die face (die face up to 800 × 600 mm — CostVision engineering heuristic, not sourced (no tilt machine's platen size was read)); the 2-up die's steel 230.6 kg ≤ 250 kg (the tilt machine's maximum mould, K5 — Made-in-China (Quanzhou Jingda): tilting gravity machine with robot pouring, US$19,000–19,800, max mould 250 kg (C))). Castings a die opening = impressions: the cycle is a die opening, the die is priced for 1 cavity and its life is 100,000 die cycles × 1 — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impressions question: UNDECIDED — needs "How many impressions does the gravity die carry?" (One impression | Two impressions)
  shotBlastCostPerPart=0.236  [gravity castings are blasted to clean the as-cast surface — oxide and die-joint flash (no sand core is costed on the permanent mould) — 2.85 kg as cast (finished + machining stock) ÷ 600 kg/h (the low end of a 0.5–2 t/h tumble / hanger blast; engineering-typical, not sourced) × (blast machine £25.07/h + operator £24.60/h), min £0.10 = £0.2360 (CostVision engineering heuristic) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impregnationCostPerPart=0  [not pressure-tight — no impregnation — deterministic, use verbatim]
  impregnation question=no  [not pressure-tight — not asked — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ndtCostPerPart=0  [not safety-critical — no radiography — deterministic, use verbatim]
  manning=0.25  [100,000 castings a year ≥ 50,000 (the threshold is CostVision engineering judgement, not sourced) → a multi-machine gravity cell (dosing / robot ladle, extraction portal): crew 0.25 operator a machine — one operator to four machines — G3 — Foundry-Planet (Gauss cell, Wuling, 2011): 11 cylinder heads an hour a machine, one operator "operates on four machines" (C); a robot-tended rotary table is one operator a table (G2 — FMT (Hall, 2009): a single tilt-pour machine "12-30 cycles per hour" (2–5 min a die cycle); an indexing rotary table with tending robots run by one operator (C)); the robot ladle / dosing unit, holding furnace and extraction portal are NOT priced — the machine rate is one tilt machine's (no published price for them was read; research gap 4) — deterministic, use verbatim]
  leakTestSec=0  [not pressure-tight — no leak test — deterministic, use verbatim]
  ladlePreheatKwhPerT=0  [aluminium — ladle preheat is sourced for iron and steel foundries only (EU JRC SF BREF 2024, BAT-AEPL Tables 4.1 (iron) and 4.2 (steel), kWh per tonne of liquid metal); NOT costed for this metal — deterministic, use verbatim]
  dustExtractionKwhPerT=0  [aluminium — the dust-extraction figure is an iron / steel foundry's (German data restated in the EU JRC SF BREF 2024 §2.3.8.1 (flue-gas cleaning ~20 kWh per tonne of good casting)); NOT costed for this metal — deterministic, use verbatim]
  plantElectricityKwhPerT=0  [gravity aluminium — the plant-electricity figure is a green-sand iron plant's; NOT costed for this route / metal. NOT costed (no published price found): furnace and ladle refractory (8–9 kg/t molten on induction, 1994 data — no current price), the metallurgical lab a melt, the pouring crew beyond the cell crew and the melt shop's operator-hours — deterministic, use verbatim]
  finish question: UNDECIDED — needs "Is the part coated or surface-treated?" (None — bare part | E-coat / KTL (zirconium pre-treat) | Powder coat (iron phosphate pre-treat) | Vibratory mass finish (deburr))
